messages:
Sam (VP Eng): Follow-up from today: we landed on biweekly majors. Need one-page rules so teams don't guess.
Olga (Release Eng): Agreed. I'll draft a short "What is a major?" decision table. Proposal: public API, schema changes, billing, infra dependencies = major. Everything else = minor/hotfix.
Priya (Product): That decision table helps. Also request an explicit freeze timeline: 3 business days before cut for normal majors, 7 for infra-impacting ones.
Dev (SRE): Operational rules: canary minimum 4h, staged ramp plan, and 48h post-rollout watch. Auto-incident if error_rate delta > 0.4% or p99 > baseline * 1.3.
Rita (QA): QA rules for majors: no open criticals, smoke pass on staging, full regression on staging, and top-150 prompt eval < 3% regression. Will publish a one-pager with a copyable command.
Maya (Eng Ops): I'll add ticket fields: release_type, freeze_date, release_owner, rollback_contact, cs_notice. Also craft a short customer notice template (72h heads-up).
Olga (Release Eng): Suggest adding a release-day checklist: pre-freeze smoke, run canary tests, verify metrics at 15/60/240m, then post-rollout 24h summary. I'll add that to the template.
Sam (VP Eng): Leadership asks: keep majors predictable, minimise customer impact, and keep hotfixes fast. Ops + Release + QA to finalise the one-pager by Thursday.
deploy-bot: "Planned canary: 8% at 14:00 UTC. Monitor p95/p99/error-rate. Rollback thresholds active."
Priya (Product): I'll schedule a 30m sync Wed to review the one-pager with owners.
Maya (Eng Ops): Owners recap: Olga (decision table + release checklist), Rita (QA checklist + harness link), Dev (monitoring + rollback automation), Maya (ticket fields + customer template), Priya (PM coordination). I'll drop the draft in Confluence and ping for review.
Sam (VP Eng): Thanks all, good follow-up. Closing thread ; will post links after Docs review.
